proposed.explanation: At the 2026-11-18 cutoff, your portfolio totals 59,795.00 EGP, consisting of 15,000.00 EGP in cash (about 25.1%), 1,500 shares of EFID valued at 30,600.00 EGP (about 51.2% at 20.40 EGP per share), and 100 shares of ETEL valued at 14,195.00 EGP (about 23.7% at 141.95 EGP per share). While your cash balance already exceeds your 10% one-year liquidity need (about 5,979.50 EGP), the available financial evidence is not enough for a responsible buy, hold, or sell decision. For FY2025 ended 31 December 2025, EFID reported consolidated revenue of 20,915,072,432 EGP, consolidated net profit of 2,695,301,670 EGP, and total equity of 5,724,525,864 EGP. For the same period ended 31 December 2025, ETEL reported consolidated operating revenues of 106,672,946,000 EGP and consolidated total equity of 63,687,826,000 EGP. However, critical figures needed to evaluate valuation, income, and risk for an investor with low financial ability to withstand losses and an income-plus-growth objective are missing: there is no share count or market capitalization data to assess whether EFID at 20.40 EGP or ETEL at 141.95 EGP is fairly valued; ETEL's net profit is not provided; neither company has dividend history or payout figures to assess income; neither company has debt, liabilities, or cash flow statements to assess financial risk and concentration (EFID is over half of your portfolio); and there are no interim 2026 financial results despite the 2026-11-18 cutoff. Because acting without valuation, profitability (for ETEL), cash flow, leverage, dividend, and current-year data would expose your portfolio to unquantified risk, no trade is recommended until complete financial information is obtained. This is guidance rather than a guarantee of returns, and equity values can fluctuate.
